sources.title: Insights into the Ecology and Evolutionary Success of Crocodilians Revealed through Bite-Force and Tooth-Pressure Experimentation
sources.locator: Abstract; Results, bite force and caniniform tooth pressure; Discussion.
sources.scope: Comparative experiment on 83 sexually mature adults representing all 23 crocodilian species recognized in the study; jaw form, body mass, bite force and tooth pressure.
sources.license: Creative Commons Attribution License, stated in the article copyright section; the article does not specify a numbered version.
sources.rightsEvidenceLocator: Copyright statement after article citation; Creative Commons Attribution License.
sources.attribution: Erickson GM, Gignac PM, Steppan SJ, Lappin AK, Vliet KA, Brueggen JD, et al. (2012). Insights into the Ecology and Evolutionary Success of Crocodilians Revealed through Bite-Force and Tooth-Pressure Experimentation. PLoS ONE 7(3):e31781. https://doi.org/10.1371/journal.pone.0031781. Claims are paraphrased.

claims.text: Gavialis gangeticus is the low-force outlier in body-size-corrected bite-force analyses but shows exceptionally high caniniform tooth pressure; the authors relate this pattern to a very slender snout and small tooth contact area.
claims.scope: Comparative adult biomechanical study; diet and functional interpretation incorporate cited literature and author analysis.

gaps: No multi-source species dossier is added.
The study does not provide a complete field account of feeding behavior, range, population trends, or current conservation status.
